sections.heading: Where Troopers Write Tickets in El Paso County
paragraphs: The Texas DPS Highway Patrol covers the state highways in and around El Paso, and troopers write a large share of the county's speeding tickets. The heaviest enforcement is on I-10 from Anthony and Vinton through downtown and out past Horizon City, and on US-54, the Patriot Freeway, running north past Fort Bliss. Loop 375 — the Border Highway, the Joe Battle stretch and the Transmountain segment — is a regular radar location, as are TX-20 (Alameda and Mesa) and Montana Avenue, US-62/180, as it opens up east of the city.

Troopers also work the rural roads most El Paso drivers only see on weekends: Montana out to Hueco Tanks, the two-lane highways toward Dell City, and the farm-to-market roads through San Elizario and Clint. Those are long, straight roads with 65 and 70 mph limits where speeds drift up, and a trooper running stationary radar from a crossover sees you a mile out.

The citation itself looks different from an El Paso Police ticket: it is a DPS form, and the court listed on it is a Justice of the Peace precinct, not Municipal Court downtown. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case.

sections.heading: Trooper Tickets Go to Justice of the Peace Court, Not Municipal Court
paragraphs: This is the detail that trips people up. El Paso Police tickets go to El Paso Municipal Court on Overland. Trooper tickets, like Sheriff's Office and constable tickets, are filed in one of the El Paso County Justice of the Peace precincts, depending on where the stop happened. A ticket on I-10 near Vinton and one on Loop 375 near Socorro are heard by different judges in different buildings with different docket schedules.

JP courts run differently from Municipal Court. Dockets are smaller, the judge is often directly involved in plea discussions, and the county attorney's office prosecutes. Knowing which precinct your case is in, and how that judge handles deferred disposition, is a large part of what you're paying a local lawyer for.

Our flat fee for any trooper ticket in a JP court is $69. If the trooper wrote more than one citation — speeding plus no insurance or expired registration is the classic pair — each additional ticket is a discounted add-on handled on the same docket.

sections.heading: Dashcam, Bodycam and Why Troopers Show Up
paragraphs: DPS traffic stops are recorded. The dashcam captures the approach, the radar or lidar reading and your vehicle; the bodycam captures the conversation at your window. That video cuts both ways. It can confirm a speed reading, or it can show a trooper pacing from too far back, a reading taken on a different vehicle in heavy traffic, or a statement at the window that doesn't match the citation.

The other difference is attendance. In Municipal Court, a case sometimes resolves because the city officer is on leave, has transferred or doesn't appear. Troopers are scheduled to court in blocks and reliably appear, and the county attorney knows it. Hoping the officer no-shows is a poor strategy against DPS. The better approach is to request the video and device records, find the real weaknesses, and negotiate from them at the pretrial setting.

sections.heading: Negotiating a Trooper Ticket at the First JP Setting
paragraphs: When you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we identify the precinct from your citation and file a notice of appearance with that JP court promptly, so the appearance date stops being a failure-to-appear risk. We request the trooper's report, the video and the device records, and review the citation for defects.

Because the trooper will be available, the result usually comes from negotiation rather than a dismissal for non-appearance. Deferred disposition is a common outcome we work for: a court fee, a clean deferral period, and a dismissal with no conviction. Drivers who qualify can often use a defensive driving dismissal. For speeds 25 mph or more over, where the course is generally unavailable, we ask for an amended charge that insurers don't rate the same way. Our goal is to pursue the best available outcome based on the citation, driving record, court and circumstances. You generally do not need to appear. Se habla español.

sections.heading: Common Trooper Citations and What They Cost You
paragraphs: The large majority of trooper tickets are speeding, and interstate speeds tend to be higher: 80 in a 65 on I-10, 85 or 90 on the open stretches of Montana. The fine for most Transportation Code violations is capped at $200, plus court costs set by the court, but the number that matters is the moving-violation conviction on your record. A conviction may affect insurance premiums depending on your history, carrier and other rating factors. Texas no longer uses the former Driver Responsibility Program points system; DPS may suspend the license of a "habitual violator" — four or more moving-violation convictions arising from separate incidents within 12 consecutive months, or seven or more within 24 months (Transp. Code §521.292(b)).

Troopers also write a lot of paperwork tickets — expired registration, no insurance, no driver's license — and enforce the state texting ban on the highways. Commercial drivers get particular attention: DPS handles most CDL and trucking inspections on I-10, and those cases carry employment consequences that make a $69 flat fee a small price.

sections.heading: Find the Precinct on Your Citation, Then Send It In
paragraphs: Read the citation and find the court: it names a Justice of the Peace precinct and an appearance deadline. Don't pay it online, don't request defensive driving yourself, and don't miss the date. Write down what the trooper said about the speed and how it was measured, the lane you were in, and the traffic around you. On I-10 at rush hour, which vehicle the radar actually clocked is a fair question.

If the deadline already passed, the JP court has likely issued a warrant. Use the free ticket and warrant lookup or go straight to our warrant recall page and call us the same day. Otherwise, send us the citation (both sides, so we can read the precinct and the deadline), your driver's license, your insurance card, your notes about the stop, and any companion citations the trooper wrote. That is all we need to start.

faqs.q: Which court handles a DPS trooper ticket in El Paso?
faqs.a: A Justice of the Peace precinct in El Paso County, not El Paso Municipal Court. The precinct depends on where on the highway the stop occurred, and it is printed on the citation. We handle trooper tickets in every El Paso County JP precinct for a flat $69.

faqs.q: Is a trooper ticket harder to fight than a city police ticket?
faqs.a: It calls for a different approach. Troopers reliably appear and their stops are recorded, so a case rarely resolves on a no-show. Instead we request the dashcam and device records, find the weak points, and negotiate at the pretrial setting.

faqs.q: Can I get the trooper's dashcam video?
faqs.a: Generally, yes. The video is part of the case file and is obtained through the county attorney's office. We request it in contested trooper cases, along with the radar or lidar calibration records.

faqs.q: Will I have to drive to the JP court?
faqs.a: Generally not. We file the appearance, handle the pretrial negotiation and report the result. That is especially useful when the precinct is on the far side of the county from where you live.

faqs.q: I was going 25+ over on I-10. What are my options?
faqs.a: The defensive driving dismissal is generally unavailable at that speed, and JP judges treat high interstate speeds seriously. We negotiate for deferred disposition where the judge allows it, and otherwise for an amended, non-moving charge so the high speed does not reach your record or your insurer.

faqs.q: The trooper gave me two tickets at the same stop. Is that two fees?
faqs.a: The first ticket is $69 and each additional citation from the same stop is added at a discounted rate shown at checkout. Both are resolved together on the same JP docket, which is also how we negotiate them — as one case.
